chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When Udayy ibn Hatim arrived at the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) brought him into his house. There was in the house nothing except a sack and a pillow of leather. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spread it for Udayy ibn Hatim.'

key_terms.أَدَمٍ: Leather (specifically from a cow or similar animal)
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.خَصَفَةٍ: A simple sack or mat used for sitting or sleeping
key_terms.عَدِيُّ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ: Udayy ibn Hatim, a companion known for his conversion and eloquence

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) do when a guest arrived and his house had very few possessions?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) profound humility (*tawadu'*) and generosity (*karam*) by offering his only bedding to Udayy ibn Hatim, a prominent chief who had recently embraced Islam. In Shia scholarly tradition, this incident is often cited to illustrate the virtue of honoring guests even in poverty, serving as a practical model for the Ahl al-Bayt's own ascetic lifestyle and their emphasis on social etiquette (*adab*) as a manifestation of faith.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Al Alawy, from his father, from his grandfather who said,

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When Udayy Bin Hatim proceeded to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> entered him into his<sup>saww</sup> house, and there did not happen to be in the house apart from a sack and a pillow of animal skin. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> placed it for him’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah al-‘Alawi from his father from his grandfather who has said the following:

“Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘When ‘Adi ibn Hatim came to the Holy Prophet, he brought him (‘Adi) to his house. In his house there was nothing to use as a seat except a sack (storage for dates) and a pillow made of animal skin. With such items the Messenger of Allah prepared a seat for ‘Adi ibn Hatim.’”
